# Drawing text with retained page fields

`control.docx` is an independently authored, deterministic fixture generated by
`tools/drawing_text_fields_fixture.py` from our drawing-text control. It contains
three standalone/grouped text frames with PAGE, NUMPAGES and SECTIONPAGES fields,
simple and complex envelopes, locked and unlocked fields, and two identical
adjacent PAGE atoms. The deliberately cached result is `99`.

`native-edited.docx` is the separate reference SaveAs2 result. The reference application
replaced the neighboring `Before` text with `Edited` in each frame.
`native-edits.json` records the unchanged source hash and the five field codes,
cached results and locks before and after. The recording tool binds to the exact
already-open source and uses the reference application's text-frame story ranges. It neither changes
the original fixture nor controls unrelated documents. These are our authored
artifacts; no corpus artwork or font programs are included.

The editor draft displays a cached field result as one atomic model character.
Neighboring text can be edited and whole atoms deleted. Retained field envelopes
are preserved during serialization; duplicate, new or altered fields and field
formatting changes are rejected. Field code/result authoring, nested fields and
other field families remain unsupported. Physical page-field evaluation remains
on the existing page-story/drawing rendering path, separate from the draft cache.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 provisions: §§17.16.5.42 (NUMPAGES), 17.16.5.44 (PAGE),
17.16.5.55 (SECTIONPAGES), 17.16.18 (fldChar), and 17.16.19 (fldSimple).

`tests/drawing-text-fields.test.js` verifies atomic layout stops, native evidence,
adjacent field identity, guarded edits, package preservation and exact undo.
`tests/browser/drawing-text-fields.spec.js` exercises the actual drawing-text
menu, field-format rollback, Apply, download, reopen, undo and redo in all frames.
Schema validation covers both source and native result; it does not certify all
OOXML semantics or pixel fidelity. Hashes are recorded in `hashes.json`.
